about.title: Bakersfield Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Bakersfield moves on wide, fast surface streets, and that shapes how crashes happen here. In 2025, the city recorded 1,436 injury collisions, with 2,245 people hurt and 36 lives lost. Public records show the highest collision counts along Union Avenue, White Lane, Panama Lane, and Ming Avenue, and reports tend to cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters and weekend traffic overlap. If one of those numbers now describes your week, the paperwork that follows can feel like a second collision. LawProactive exists to take one task off your plate. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Kern County residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You tell us what happened; we make the introduction. From there, the attorney can review fault, deal with the insurers, and keep track of California's two-year filing deadline while you focus on getting better.

items.title: Deadlines tracked from day one
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim involving a city, county, or state vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. The attorney you're matched with knows which clock applies to your case.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't shut the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame; your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: No fee unless you recover
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car crash claim. Our connection service costs you nothing.

items.question: The other driver's insurer keeps calling for a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: Politely decline until you've spoken with an attorney. Recorded statements are often used to lock you into early details before your injuries are fully known. You can confirm the crash happened and share your own insurer's information without going on the record about fault or how you feel.

items.question: I was hit on White Lane by a driver in a City of Bakersfield vehicle. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can. Claims against a government entity in California generally require a formal claim within six months, far shorter than the usual two-year window. Because that deadline moves fast, it's worth getting connected with an attorney soon so the notice is filed correctly and on time.

items.question: What should I save from the scene of a Bakersfield crash?
items.answer: Keep photos of the vehicles, the intersection, skid marks, and your injuries, along with the police report number and contact details for any witnesses. Hold on to medical records, repair estimates, and receipts, and avoid repairing or selling your car before it's been documented. Nearby businesses along corridors like Ming Avenue may have camera footage, but it's often overwritten within days, so an attorney will want to request it early.
